arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Sean Summers argued the funeral context makes the speech harmful.
He stated the family wanted a private, dignified burial.
He claimed the protesters made that impossible.
Justice Scalia questioned if the claim relies solely on the location.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the limits of free speech near a funeral. The family wants compensation for distress. The protesters want legal immunity for their message.

paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between private grief and public speech. It determines when courts can award damages for offensive words. It balances individual rights against community standards.
